newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa likely to begin navy purchases soon.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa likely to begin navy purchases soon.

text.p: South Africa's cabinet will be asked to approve buying four corvettes and several submarines next month, with the aquisition process starting immediately after that, Defence Minister Joe Modise said on Friday.
Asked if he was confident approval would be forthcoming, he told reporters that deals now being discussed were too good to pass up.
"It's tantamount to us getting some of this equipment for nothing," he said.

"A number of countries are...coming with attractive packages that are going to result in us getting back the exact amount we are paying on the equipment in the form of investments in South Africa," he said without naming any countries.
Modise's deputy, Ronnie Kasrils, said earlier this year that Britain, whose Yarrow shipyard is among favoured contenders, had made "interesting" proposals for such a package.
Modise said the investments would be aimed at job creation and many of the foreign companies involved were interested in investing in South Africa's defence industries.
"Naturally we would like them to buy an equity. Secondly, we would like them to bring in technology. Thirdly, we would like to share their markets with them," he said.
"There's no point in bringing technology into our industries when we cannot sell the equipment we are going to produce."
He said a comprehensive review of South Africa's defence needs was now complete.

"Now in June, we're looking at the force design and how it should be equipped, and once that has been accepted by cabinet and parliament, we can go ahead and begin the process of acquisition," he said.
Modise said contracts would include a penalty clause to ensure the foreign investment performed.
"Over the duration of the period that we're paying, we'll be monitoring the industries that they've invested in....If the industry does not perform, then there is a penalty they will have to pay."
